run.question: How does /afk:execute Step 10.5 start /afk:adversary and consume its verdict today (a fresh session or subagent blind to the reasoning, diff and tests, respawn on tainted or env_unreachable capped at 2, the {slug}-adversary.md report and the ADVERSARY: line), what else reaches the adversary, and what breaks if the adversary becomes a new pane agent for each attempt that keeps its blind diet, writes its own named report, and sends finished into its requester's pane instead of returning its verdict as the spawn call's result? Premise: Only the contact may message a pane adversary, and Stop-gate output reaches it only after its verdict is recorded. Premise: A pane adversary writes a checkpoint in the run; a replacement after a death reads it, and a fresh attempt after tainted does not. Premise: S-239's reader rule binds the running run only; a report under plan/review/ that the stage names keeps its stage's readers.

Today execute Step 10.5 starts the adversary by running /afk:adversary {NNNN-slug} {app-base-url} in a fresh session or subagent that has not seen the run's reasoning, diff or tests, once an app instance serving the slice is up, booted through app-start-gate.sh when the invoker did not provision one (execute/SKILL.md:89). The skill takes only those two arguments (adversary/SKILL.md:14-15) and must not read the slice diff, the implementor's tests, review findings or any commit of the branch; if any enters its context it reports tainted (adversary/SKILL.md:19-21).

Today execute reads the adversary's verdict from the spawning call's own result and never from a completion notification; a child returning nothing usable is recorded as 'no verdict' and the run continues (execute/SKILL.md:135). The adversary writes its full report to plan/review/{NNNN-slug}-adversary.md, overwritten on a re-run, and ends with the line 'ADVERSARY: <clean|findings|tainted|env_unreachable> — probed=<n> …' and an 'In plain terms' line (adversary/SKILL.md:40-44); in driven mode an orchestrator parses the trailing status line (REPORTING.md:13).

Execute routes the verdict: clean goes to Step 11; findings with any critical or high are remediated by class and re-run from Step 8 under their own cap of 2, then adversary_fail; medium or low only are advisories; tainted or env_unreachable respawn fresh or restore the app and re-run, capped at 2 such attempts, then adversary_fail naming the taint or blocked(env_unreachable); a run that ends before the gate can spawn stops with adversary_unrun (execute/SKILL.md:91-95, :118-119). Every gate verdict is journalled as 'adversary {verdict} …' (execute/SKILL.md:37, skills/afk/to-subtasks/JOURNAL-FORMAT.md:33).

The report plan/review/{slug}-adversary.md is read by file name or folder: mission control's gates and insights sections glob *-adversary.md and parse a 'verdict' label in the first 4000 characters (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/gates.py:110-120, skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/insights.py:204-233), the progress section shows 'adversary probed' when the file exists (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/progress.py:75, skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/assets/shell.html:932), the overview counts the reports (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/overview.py:143, :161); /afk:retro mines verdicts and finding classes (skills/afk/retro/SKILL.md:29); /afk:understand reads plan/review/*.md and mines it for deviations (skills/afk/understand/SKILL.md:49, :58); the review rollup mentions it (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:167); the adversary_fail next action points at it (README.md:588); /afk:gc deletes plan/ whole after the merge (skills/afk/gc/SKILL.md:53).

Given the premise that a report under plan/review/ that the stage names keeps its stage's readers, every reader of the adversary report is unchanged: the change keeps the report's name and folder (S-209, GRILL-LOG.md:561; S-173, :525; S-198, :550), so mission control, /afk:retro, /afk:understand, the review rollup and /afk:gc read or delete it as today.

The ADVERSARY: line is parsed only by execute, from the spawn result (execute/SKILL.md:135; REPORTING.md:13). Mission control's regexes need a 'verdict' or '**Verdict:**' label (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/gates.py:21-25, skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/insights.py:30-35) that the line does not carry; /afk:retro and /afk:understand read the report file whatever it holds (retro/SKILL.md:29, understand/SKILL.md:49), and adversary/SKILL.md:40 does not say whether 'End with:' puts the line in the file or only in the final message. After the change finished carries only a format version and the result path (S-231, GRILL-LOG.md:666), so the line reaches execute only if the report file carries it. The draft's 'ADVERSARY: line unchanged' holds for the grammar, not for the channel.

Today execute takes the verdict from the spawn result and the findings from the report file: routing remediation by each finding's class (execute/SKILL.md:92) and the adversary_fail outcome naming each finding's class and repro path (execute/SKILL.md:118) need the fields each finding carries (adversary/SKILL.md:37), which the adversary writes to the report (adversary/SKILL.md:40), while its closing lines carry only the verdict, the severity counts and the report path (adversary/SKILL.md:43-44).

The draft's 'finished goes into its requester's pane' (S-189) holds only by default: the current PRD delivers a role's finished message to the report target the manifest and pattern name, whatever target the sender wrote, with a copy to the contact agent, and the target is the asker only where the pattern names none (PRD.md:148-149, AC-048 and AC-049; S-212, GRILL-LOG.md:607). An execute running inside the contact session receives messages in the contact's inbox, not its pane (S-215, GRILL-LOG.md:618; S-189, :541).

At HEAD the harness refusal does not block the adversary's own report write: on Claude Code a subagent's Write was refused for REPORT.md, SUMMARY.md and findings.md, but the same subagent wrote 0001-x-adversary.md, the adversary report's name shape; on Codex no name was refused (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:329, in the pane-agent probes of 2026-09-30 on the versions named at :308-310). The fallback rule that makes the starter write a subagent's report file (PRD.md:144 AC-044; S-157, GRILL-LOG.md:462) is therefore not needed for the adversary's file name, and applying it moves the write of plan/review/{slug}-adversary.md to execute, against execute's ownership rule (execute/SKILL.md:143) and the plan/review/ co-writer list that names /afk:adversary's report files (CLAUDE.md:160, AGENTS.md:160). execute/SKILL.md:89 breaks: a pane adversary is started by the contact agent, directly when execute runs in the contact session and through a start request from any other agent (S-153, GRILL-LOG.md:458), with every duty, the slug, the app URL and the run mode in its launch prompt (S-150, :455; start body S-231, :666). A Claude pane agent's shell has no CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT or PLUGIN_ROOT (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:322; Codex unproven) while the adversary reads plugin-root doctrine before writing (adversary/SKILL.md:6, :40, :47), so the brief names those paths. execute/SKILL.md:135 breaks: it forbids waiting on a completion notification and has a child that returns nothing recorded as 'no verdict' while the run continues, but the change has execute wait for the finished message in its pane (S-189, GRILL-LOG.md:541) and learn of a lost adversary from the contact agent (S-173, :525). Pane delivery is proven on both harnesses: a busy pane agent received three sent messages in order, and a pane agent that ended its turn took a relayed answer after minutes idle (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:327-328).

adversary/SKILL.md:40 and :51 break. Given the premise that a pane adversary writes a checkpoint in the run, read by a replacement after a death and not by a fresh attempt after tainted, the checkpoint and the finished message are outputs besides the report, against 'The report is the only output' (:51). The report becomes the verdict's only path to execute, so :40 must put the ADVERSARY: line in the file, and its 'verdict line + journal carry history' leaves only execute's journal line (execute/SKILL.md:37) as history; under the fallback the adversary returns text instead of writing (AC-044).

The respawn cap is unchanged: each tainted or env_unreachable re-run becomes a new pane agent and the cap of 2 still counts attempts (execute/SKILL.md:93). Given the premise that a fresh attempt after tainted does not read the checkpoint, nothing from a tainted attempt reaches the next one; a replacement after a death resumes the session or reads the checkpoint (S-213, GRILL-LOG.md:608) and is not a re-run attempt. The draft lists :93 as a site; it does not change.

DELEGATION.md:34 and :36 break for the adversary: the stall watchdog is armed in the spawn's own message and wakes the orchestrator by exiting, because only completion re-invokes a waiting orchestrator. A pane adversary has no spawn call and no completion; the requester waits for finished (S-189) and the contact agent tells it when the agent is lost (S-173), so a hung but live pane adversary needs a bound these lines do not give.

The report itself is exempt (hooks/wiring-gate.sh:49).

Given the premise that Stop-gate output reaches a pane adversary only after its verdict is recorded, the output cannot taint the verdict, but a block can still hold the adversary's turn open: the plugin Stop gates run at a pane session's turn end on both harnesses (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:323), the dispatcher runs the wiring gate in every session and blocks again on an unchanged tree that blocked before (hooks/stop-gates.sh:34-36, :55-56, :108), the wiring gate blocks on any orphan the branch's commits added (hooks/wiring-gate.sh:104-109, :205), and in a native session a block kept blocking while the tree stayed invalid (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:23). The adversary edits nothing (adversary/SKILL.md:51), so on a branch carrying such an orphan it can end its turn only by editing the branch or not at all. A subagent adversary at HEAD never meets these gates: a subagent's end fires only SubagentStop, which hooks.json does not register (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:323). In the probe worktree the gate run passed the 300 s hook limit (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:323), and a timed-out run does not block.

Each pane turn end runs the plugin Stop gates, which in the probe worktree ran past the 300 s hook limit on both harnesses, and messages sent to a pane agent during its Stop hook wait until the hook ends (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:323, :327); a finished message to a requester inside its own Stop hook can arrive minutes late.

claims.text: Over docs/, which holds only docs/afk/agent-team-topology, a case-blind substring search for 'adversar' over tracked and untracked files returns 12570 lines. 12539 are B1 seed nodes. The other 31 are lines of prior investigation ledgers that hold the stem inside a recorded command, method or evidence string. The 240 B1 seed nodes it does not return are prior-ledger lines that carry only the step forms Step 10.5 or 10.5. So the seed's name forms missed no line of the feature documents that names the adversary.

The current feature documents send a role's finished message to its report target, which the run takes from the manifest and the pattern whatever target the sender wrote, with a copy to the contact agent's inbox; the asker is the target only when the pattern names none (S-212 GRILL-LOG.md:607, S-235 :670, AC-048 PRD.md:148, ADR-0015:8). The draft's 'finished goes into its requester's pane' (S-189, :541) is that default case, which is the adversary's case at Step 10.5 while no pattern names a target for it.

Delivery of finished into a requester's pane, and its wake, is no longer frontier when the requester is not the contact agent. Every message to such an agent goes into its pane by herdr agent prompt (S-148, GRILL-LOG.md:453). The probe rows show a busy pane agent receiving three such messages in send order on Claude Code and Codex, only after its turn or Stop hook ended (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:327). They also show an agent that ended its turn staying live and taking a relayed message after about 4 minutes idle on both (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:328). A requester busy in its own turn gets the verdict late, not lost.

When /afk:execute runs in the contact session, the agent that asks for the adversary is the contact agent, and messages to the contact land only in its inbox (S-215 GRILL-LOG.md:618, AC-046 PRD.md:146). A Claude contact wakes when its wait job ends; a Codex contact does not and takes the message at its next turn (trial T12 GRILL-LOG.md:489, S-166 :492, AC-065 PRD.md:165). Under a Codex contact, Step 10.5 then waits for the human's next message, where today the spawn call returns the verdict within the same turn (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:135).

S-235 (GRILL-LOG.md:670) delivers finished to the pane of the report target, then to the contact agent's inbox, and has no case for a target that is the contact agent itself. For an adversary that the contact session started, that order sends the message into the contact's pane, which AC-046 (PRD.md:146) bars. The rows that fill the manifest's requester field (S-179 :531, S-220 :623) do not say what it holds for a start outside a pattern. The design must state where finished goes in that case.

With no stage-map entry and no picked pattern, the default, a Step 10.5 run outside the contact session has no valid way to start its pane adversary. An example is the /afk:autopilot subtask agent, itself a role spawn (S-208, GRILL-LOG.md:560). It must send a start request (S-153, :458). The request needs a pattern step, with no default (S-179 :531, S-220 :623). The run refuses an unknown step with exit code 2 (S-187 :539; AC-042 PRD.md:142). Yet the pane default needs nothing configured (AC-041 PRD.md:141, ADR-0013:18). AC-032 says such a stage runs as it does today (PRD.md:132), which ADR-0013:18 says holds only with the switch set back or no pane transport. The design must give a role spawn outside a pattern its own path, or keep a subagent adversary when no pattern is resolved.

Outside the contact session, every adversary attempt starts through a start request to the contact agent, and a role agent waits for the contact agent's turn to end (ADR-0013:18). A Codex contact takes worker messages only at its next turn (S-166, GRILL-LOG.md:492). So under a Codex contact, each start, including each respawn after tainted or env_unreachable, waits for the human's next message. Today the agent running the gate spawns the adversary itself within its turn (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:89).

SDD.md:771, repeated at line 1108 of the refused draft, marks the stage-skill spawn points 'unchanged with no map entry' and 'extends'. But S-199 classes the Step 10.5 adversary as reworked (GRILL-LOG.md:551), and ADR-0013:18 makes every role spawn change with nothing configured. So the row is wrong for the adversary's spawn, and the draft's adversary row (line 1118) does not list it.

Given the premise that a replacement after a death reads the pane adversary's checkpoint and a fresh attempt after tainted does not, the checkpoint rule breaks as written. It keeps one checkpoint per role per run, at a path built from the feature and the role, and lets the next agent in that role read it (PRD.md:175, S-239 GRILL-LOG.md:674). That reader includes the fresh attempt, which would then start from what the tainted attempt saved. The rule needs a separate checkpoint per attempt, or a reset on tainted. Like every S-239 rule, it holds only by the agents' briefs, because no program sees a file read (:674, ADR-0016:8).

Given the premise that S-239's reader rule binds the running run only, its rule that only the report target reads a result file (GRILL-LOG.md:674, PRD.md:174) does not reach the adversary's report. The gate names that report under plan/review/ (S-173 :525, S-209 :561), and cleanup leaves it to its stage's lifetime (S-198 :550). The stage's readers keep reading it.

The PRD puts a pattern verifier in the fresh adversary session (PRD.md:207), and the patterns proposal makes build-verify's verifier that session (PATTERNS-PROPOSAL.md:136). But the proposal's verifier runs the verification tiers and the adversary probe in one agent (:142, :170). Its flowchart draws an edge from the builder into it (:142), and in afk-lite it talks to the orchestrator and the builder for a whole step (:184). The adversary's diet bars the implementor's tests (skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:21). Given the premise that only the contact may message a pane adversary, that verifier cannot be the pane adversary as drawn. It also cannot be a new agent for each attempt while it lives for the whole step. The proposal must split the probe from the tiers and drop the message edges into it.

The refused draft's adversary row (line 1118) lists as impacted flows only skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:40 and skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:89, 93 and 135. Among the feature documents, it misses these rows that the change contradicts: the spawn-point row SDD.md:771; AC-032 PRD.md:132; the start-request checks AC-042 PRD.md:142, S-187 GRILL-LOG.md:539 and S-220 :623; the checkpoint rule PRD.md:175 with S-239 :674; S-235's missing contact-target case (:670); and the pattern verifier (PATTERNS-PROPOSAL.md:136, :142, :170, :184). Its Conventions cell cites S-189 for the delivery, which the later S-212 and S-235 limit to the default report target.

With no pattern, the adversary has no declared talk edge, so the PRD's message rule lets only the contact agent that started it send it a message (PRD.md:173). That matches the premise that only the contact may message a pane adversary. It holds by the agents' briefs only, since no agent identity reaches a hook (ADR-0016:8).

Under /afk:autopilot today, Step 10.5 asks the subtask subagent to start the adversary, a third level of agents. Autopilot spawns that subagent with SUBAGENT-PROMPT.md (autopilot/SKILL.md:33), and none of the brief's 41 lines states the depth it may spawn at; the SDD records the same gap, that no stage-skill spawn states its depth (SDD.md:620). DELEGATION.md:29 has a child without that statement run its helper work inline, and Codex has no depth contract, so its children run helpers inline (CAPABILITIES.md:15, PROVIDERS.md:71). An adversary run inline by the subtask agent has seen the diff and breaks its own diet (adversary/SKILL.md:21). So the subagent spawn that execute/SKILL.md:89 asks for has no sanction in the doctrine on Claude Code and no support on Codex. Where AC-032 governs, a stage with no human present runs as today (PRD.md:132, :275) and the autopilot path keeps this gap; where ADR-0013:18 governs, the start moves to the contact agent instead.

The draft's adversary row does not list adversary/SKILL.md:47, and the change reaches it. That line has the adversary render its findings as the RP-4 table when a human is present, and use the written report in driven mode. Execute starts the adversary with only the slug and the app URL (execute/SKILL.md:89; adversary/SKILL.md:14-15), so the adversary decides for itself whether a human is present. No line read settles that for a pane adversary started in an interactive run. If it reads itself as human-present, it must render (LAVISH.md:386-391), and a render waits on a poll with no timeout (LAVISH.md:374-378). Its finished message would then wait until a person answers the findings page.

Outside docs/, 16 lines reach the adversary with no seed name form and no 'adversar' stem, so neither the seed's pass nor a case-blind stem search returns them: mission control's verdict regexes, severity rule and colour map (gates.py:22, insights.py:31, :214, shell.html:276); the glossary definition (GLOSSARY.md:316); the RP-4 render row and the RP-4 and blind-gate tooltips (LAVISH.md:84, hooks/lavish-tips.json:44, :114); the verdict-read rule and its history (execute/SKILL.md:135, CHANGELOG.md:376, :1272); the README entry's second line (README.md:705); and the skill's own diet, env_unreachable and render lines (adversary/SKILL.md:10, :21, :38, :47). A complete list of the adversary's readers needs its verdict tokens, its render point and its diet terms as name forms.

claims.text: A wait rule specific to a Codex contact cannot be written into execute/SKILL.md or adversary/SKILL.md as it stands. The native contract gate scans every Markdown file except PROVIDERS.md, CAPABILITIES.md and providers/CONFORMANCE.md, and refuses the names Codex and Claude Code and the tool names SendMessage and subagent_type unless an allow-list line explains the exception (hooks/native-contract-gate.sh:78-82, :114-120). It runs at Stop and before a commit (CLAUDE.md:201). So a harness-specific wait for the adversary's finished message belongs in CAPABILITIES.md's degradation column, with the skill pointing at it.

The boot path that execute/SKILL.md:89 names keeps the app up only when APP_START_KEEP=1 is set: on success app-start-gate.sh kills the process it started unless that variable is 1 (adapters/build-gate/maven/app-start-gate.sh:14-16, :209). Line 89 does not mention the variable; autopilot's subtask agent sets it (autopilot/SKILL.md:36). The app-start gate exists only for the maven build kind, and the npm kind has lint and worktree-provision only (ADAPTERS.md:112, :134-135), so outside maven Step 10.5 depends on an instance the invoker provides. The planned change does not touch this path.

No test pins how mission control reads an adversary report. The only file its tests write under review/ is INDEX.md (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/tests/test_contract.py:233-236), and the seed's name-form passes put no hit in that test folder. The verdict regexes, the severity rule and the colour map (gates.py:22, :110; insights.py:31, :204, :214; shell.html:276) are therefore unguarded: if the change rewrites the head of the report, for example to carry the ADVERSARY: line without a 'verdict' label, the dashboard's verdict cells go blank and no test goes red.

Adding an outcome status for an adversary that started but never sent finished is a lockstep change. The outcome status set binds execute's Step 13 list and every skill that names a status (CLAUDE.md:135, AGENTS.md:135), and a status token is broadened only in its owning skill's file (REPORTING.md:29). Mission control flags exit statuses from a fixed list holding adversary_fail and adversary_unrun (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/insights.py:24), so a new token goes unflagged until that list changes in the same commit. Today execute records 'no verdict' and continues instead (execute/SKILL.md:135).

Given the premise that Stop-gate output reaches a pane adversary only after its verdict is recorded, the repository's own Stop gates also run at each of its turn ends, beside the plugin's: the Stop array holds a second entry that runs the repository's list under its own 300-second limit (hooks/hooks.json:63-68, hooks/hooks.codex.json:65), and Stop fires in a pane session on both harnesses (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:323). This repository's list is empty (.afk/hooks.json), so whether a consuming repository's Stop gate blocks and holds the adversary's turn open lies outside this repository.

A hung pane adversary is not left without a stall bound, but the bound acts differently on fire. The feature documents give every working agent a 20-minute stall watchdog held by the contact agent (SDD.md:588), turned off by finished or a park and armed again on resume (S-142 GRILL-LOG.md:428, S-188 :540, S-106 :365). Step 10.5 arms no watchdog itself (execute/SKILL.md:88-95 names none); DELEGATION.md:34 asks for one on every spawn whose child can run past about 15 minutes. Today a silent child is stopped and the invoking skill takes its park or fail path (DELEGATION.md:37). Under S-241 (GRILL-LOG.md:676) the contact agent leaves a silent live agent working and tells the human once, and an agent whose output shows it waits for a message also stays working. So an adversary that hangs alive leaves its requester waiting for finished, and none of the 54 lines of the case-blind watchdog search over the feature documents (q-a947c269) ends that wait without a person.

claims.text: The feature documents disagree on whether a run with no team changes the adversary's start, and the draft's row takes one side without listing the other. S-199 (GRILL-LOG.md:551, R-42) classes the Step 10.5 adversary as reworked under the decision that role agents are pane agents, and ADR-0013:18 says a plugin-enabled session with a pane transport changes behaviour with no configuration. The later posture S-246 (GRILL-LOG.md:681, R-46) says a session that uses no team sees no change and a stage with no pattern follows the rules of today; the three changes it lets an existing caller see are the configuration reader, the delegation model rules and a parked agent's watchdog. AC-032 and its note say the same for no pattern or no human present (PRD.md:132, :275), and S-230 (GRILL-LOG.md:665) holds both 'a stage with no entry runs as today' and 'no key means pane when a pane tool is found'. The draft's adversary row (its line 1118) makes every attempt a pane agent with no condition, so it contradicts S-246, AC-032 and PRD.md:275, and lists none of them.
